methods.label: Count games through player appearances
methods.explanation:
Each of the six players plays five games, one against each other player. Thus there are \(6\cdot5=30\) player appearances in games. Each game has two players, so this counts every game exactly twice. The number of games is therefore
\[
\frac{6\cdot5}{2}=15.
\]
Because there are no ties, each game contributes exactly one win. The five listed players won
\[
4+3+2+2+2=13
\]
games altogether. Monica must have won the remaining \(15-13=\boxed{2}\) games, choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: The factor of two is explained using ordinary player appearances. Only elementary multiplication, division, and subtraction are needed.
